Thanks Marissa — looping in the engineering team. We reproduced the issue and attached a short log file (finlytics-logs-20260320.zip) and a minimal repro payload. Summary:

- Symptom: Intermittent 502 / 504 from Redwood reranker endpoint while sending batched embeddings for reranking. Smaller batches (<=32) succeed consistently; batches >= 96 start failing ~30-40% of attempts.
- When it fails we see a 502 upstream gateway response. Example in logs:

[2026-03-20T17:45:21Z] ERROR upstream: recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer) while reading response header from upstream, client: 34.82.12.19, server: rerank.prod.redwood.ai, request: "POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.0.2.45:8080/", host: "rerank.prod.redwood.ai"

- Repro steps (condensed):
  1) Using our node SDK we call embeddings.batch(...) to get embeddings for 128 items.
  2) We then POST to /v1/rerank with the full batch payload (see attached repro-payload.json).
  3) Intermittent 502/504 responses; no apparent pattern by content.

Attached: repro-payload.json (small redacted sample), finlytics-logs-20260320.zip.

Let us know what additional info you need; we can keep a test deployment running and attach headers for any failing requests. Thanks.

Alex

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick repro and logs. A few requests and immediate suggestions to help narrow this down:

1) Could you paste the exact curl/SDK request (including headers) for a failing request? The x-request-id or any request-id header from the response will be very helpful.
2) As a quick mitigation, please try: reduce batch size to 32 and increase client timeout to 60s to see if the failures stop. If they do, that suggests either upstream timeouts or resource pressure on our reranker worker.
3) Can you confirm whether you are using our hosted API via region = us-west and whether you are pinning to a specific model?

A couple of things I will check on our side:
- Look for upstream gateway logs for the x-request-id you provide.
- Check worker OOM/worker restarts and connection pooling metrics for that window.

Also, as a note: if you are using structured tool-calling or function outputs in the same request payload, ensure the request shape matches the reranker contract — malformed function_call fields can cause handler exceptions. But we should be able to see exceptions in our logs with the request-id.

If you can paste the curl and a failing request-id I will prioritize this.

Thanks,

From: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@finlytics.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 14:12:05 -07:00
Subject: Root cause analysis and recommended fix (preliminary)

Team — quick update after looking through the logs for x-request-id ft-20260320-9b2c and related traces. Summary:

Findings:
- The upstream gateway (nginx) returned 502 because the backend process was closing the connection while the request body was still being read. The worker logs show an exception during deserialization when handling a very large batch payload (batch size ~128) — stack traces point to memory pressure and a sync point where the worker attempted to allocate a large buffer for embeddings + metadata. There's also evidence of socket resets from the upstream.

Immediate recommendations (short-term mitigation):
1) Ask customers to reduce batch size to 32 or 64 for now.
2) Increase client-side timeout to 60-120s depending on latency.
3) On our side: enable chunked transfer and tune nginx proxy_buffer_size / proxy_buffers to accept larger bodies without resetting.

Planned fixes (next week):
- Add streaming ingestion path for the reranker to avoid building the full in-memory payload at the worker.
- Add server-side request size warnings to return 413 instead of causing worker OOMs.
- Update SDK docs with recommended batch sizing guidance and an automatic batch-split option.

For Finlytics specifically: we can rollout a canary change to increase proxy buffers and enable chunked uploads in the next 48 hours if you want to test with your 128-batch load. If you prefer a safer route we can also add an SDK helper that splits batches automatically.

Next steps: Marissa, can we schedule a 30-min follow-up with Finlytics next week to validate the canary and plan a production rollout? Alex — if you can run one test with batch_size=64 and timeout=60s and share the response headers that'd be great.

Thanks,
Ethan
